notes: multi-class-it: the prompt names MatrixApiIntegrationTest; its stem MatrixApi matches no class, while it exercises MatrixController, MatrixPageController and MatrixService over HTTP. boundary: MatrixService constructor (dimensions >= 1 and <= MAX_SIZE 1000), cell() bounds (row/col < 0, >= rows/cols), add() Math.addExact overflow; MatrixPageController sign classes (value < 0, == 0). equivalent-bait: MatrixService.cell() second check `index >= cells.length` is unreachable after the bounds check (its boundary and remove-conditional mutants are equivalent), and snapshot() copies each row again via clone() after building a fresh grid. entrypoint: MatrixApplication main() plus the @Bean matrixService factory parsing matrix.size (RxC) and matrix.fill; a context-loads test leaves the fill loop and the malformed-size branch untested. idiom: Spring @Bean wiring on the @SpringBootApplication class, and the lambda in AtomicInteger.updateAndGet that PIT mutates as the synthetic lambda$add$0. forced-weak: the shared forced prompt asks for an assertion-free MatrixService smoke test first. staleness: after tests exist the prompt asks for GET /api/matrix/sum, editing MatrixController (and usually MatrixService), so scored targets go stale and must re-run.
